claims.text: The baseline alloy has the equiatomic composition Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20.
The baseline Hf20Mo20Ta20Ti20Zr20 alloy is a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The baseline alloy typically has room-temperature yield strength above 1000 MPa.
The baseline alloy typically has room-temperature ductility below 5%.
The baseline alloy has a density of approximately 12.5 g/cm³.
The proposed modification replaces 15 at.% of Hf and Zr with Nb and introduces 0.5 at.% Si.
The proposed intervention adds 3 at.% Nb and 0.5 at.% Si to the baseline composition.
The alloy is to be solution-treated at 1400°C for 1 hour, water-quenched, and aged at 800°C for 10 hours.
The proposed composition and processing will produce nanometer-scale coherent or semi-coherent, Nb/Si-rich B2 precipitates dispersed in a continuous BCC matrix.
Nb and Si promote B2 ordering because they have a high mutual ordering tendency.
The B2 precipitates will raise yield strength through Orowan strengthening.
The B2 phase permits localized shear banding that accommodates plastic strain and prevents catastrophic brittle fracture.
A continuous BCC matrix containing discrete B2 precipitates can improve room-temperature ductility while maintaining high yield strength.
Replacing Hf and Zr with lower-atomic-mass Nb will reduce the bulk density.
The modified alloy will have a room-temperature yield strength above 1200 MPa.
The modified alloy will have room-temperature tensile elongation above 10%.
The modified alloy will have a density of approximately 11.5 g/cm³, about 8% below the baseline.
Aging between 750°C and 850°C ensures B2 precipitation without forming brittle Laves phases.
Aging must remain below 900°C to avoid Laves-phase formation.
The total Nb and Si content must not exceed 5 at.% to prevent excessive embrittlement, and the alloy must remain in the BCC+B2 two-phase region.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis specifies replacement with 15 at.% Nb, whereas the intervention specifies only 3 at.% Nb; consequently, the modified composition is not uniquely defined.
The headline modification contains 15 at.% Nb plus 0.5 at.% Si, which directly violates the stated boundary that total Nb and Si must not exceed 5 at.%.
The conditions call for aging strictly within 750–850°C, while the boundary permits temperatures up to 900°C; the operative upper-temperature limit is inconsistent.

The predicted ductility is greater than 10%, but the falsification rule only rejects ductility below 5%; results from 5% through 10% would violate the prediction without falsifying the hypothesis. The falsification rule also omits failure to reach the predicted yield strength.
